principle: Do not confuse poor environmental condition with poor data quality.

classes.ERROR: Impossible, structurally invalid, or outside a selected instrument's hard range; blocks progression until corrected.
classes.PLAUSIBILITY_WARNING: Possible but unusual; requires attention/review and does not automatically reject.
classes.ENVIRONMENTAL_ALERT: Potentially poor water condition; does not reduce accuracy score solely because the water is unhealthy.

environmentalAlert.basis: Pennsylvania Chapter 93 general aquatic-life pH criterion

rules.notes: Generic Central-PA freshwater plausibility guardrail only. Site-designation and seasonal Pennsylvania criteria should later drive environmental alerts.

environmentalAlerts.message: Low dissolved oxygen; commonly stressful for fish.

plausibilityWarning.message: Unusually high DO concentration; review meter/context rather than reject automatically.

rules.notes: Values above 100% are allowed because supersaturation can occur.

contextWarning.message: Outside the general range EPA cites for many U.S. rivers; use site baseline before drawing conclusions.

rules.notes: High conductivity is not automatically bad data. Historical/site-specific baseline is preferred.
Use instrument/method range and site context for upper-bound review.
No universal positive/negative validity rule. Validate against selected instrument range and context.
Upper thresholds are context/use dependent; do not globally reject high values.
Do not apply criterion-based upper thresholds until method clarifies nitrate as N vs nitrate ion / combined nitrite+nitrate basis.
Method must identify phosphorus form/basis (e.g. orthophosphate, total phosphorus, as P vs as PO4) before criterion interpretation.
Zero is valid. No generic high-flow rejection; compare with site/hydrologic context.

instrumentRule: When an instrument/method profile has a documented measurement range, that hard range may be used for ERROR classification and is versioned with the rule set.
